domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study included 120 patients... group ESP (n = 40), group MTP (n = 40), and group Control (n = 40).

domain_judgments.rationale: Pain was measured consistently across groups with a standard VAS at prespecified times by a research assistant blinded to allocation, limiting differential outcome ascertainment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Postoperative pain was evaluated using a visual analogue scale (VAS 0: no pain, 10 cm: worst pain ever)... by a research assistant who was blinded to the study groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and identifies primary and secondary outcomes, but the supplied report does not establish a prespecified analysis plan for aggregating repeated VAS measurements, and many time-point and pairwise analyses leave some scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered with the Clinical Trials.gov (NCT04193488)... Primary outcome measure was mean pain scores.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by incomplete reporting of random-sequence generation, unclear participant/treating-clinician blinding and analysis by assigned group, and residual uncertainty about prespecification of the multiple pain analyses. Missing outcome data and blinded, standardized outcome measurement appear low risk.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated 1:1 using a random-number table generated through randomization.com, with the schedule placed in envelopes and opened immediately before anesthesia.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was generated by a valid random-number method and measured baseline characteristics were balanced, but concealment safeguards for the envelopes (such as sequential numbering and opacity) were not reported, and the same anesthesiologist generated the schedule and prepared the envelopes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomized (1:1) and divided into a control group...and an ultrasound-guided ESPB group...by the random number table method (www.randomization.com). The randomized schedule was hidden and generated by the anesthesiologist in charge of the case, who was not part of the study. The same anesthesiologist prepared the envelopes, and the envelopes were opened just before anesthesia.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients were under general anesthesia when the block was performed and most care was standardized, but the block performer necessarily knew allocation, no sham procedure was used, and six post-randomization exclusions led to an available-case rather than intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After general anesthesia but before surgery, patients in Group ESP received ultrasound-guided ESPB performed by the anesthesiologist who opened the randomized envelope... Following randomization, five patients were excluded because they underwent thoracotomy, and one patient was excluded due to the need for postoperative mechanical ventilation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were reported for 80 of 86 randomized participants, but six participants were excluded after randomization for post-allocation clinical events and their group distribution and outcomes were not reported, so bias from missingness cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eighty-six patients were included in the randomization. Following randomization, five patients were excluded because they underwent thoracotomy, and one patient was excluded due to the need for postoperative mechanical ventilation. Therefore, we analyzed the results of 40 patients in each group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome, cumulative sufentanil consumption recorded by a standardized PCA device, was objective and measured identically across groups, while outcome data were collected by an anesthesiologist unaware of allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome of this study was postoperative sufentanil consumption in the first 24 h... The collection of all the data was performed by the same anesthesiologist who unaware of the patients’ details and grouping.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, the primary outcome and assessment period were clearly prespecified, and the reported primary analysis corresponds to that specification, with no evident multiplicity for the primary outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered prior to patient enrollment at chictr.org.cn (identifier: ChiCTR1900022217)... The primary outcome of this study was postoperative sufentanil consumption in the first 24 h.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The main issues are incompletely described allocation concealment and exclusion of 6 of 86 randomized participants without an intention-to-treat analysis or reporting their allocation, whereas primary-outcome measurement was objective and the prospectively registered outcome was reported as planned.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly assigned to ESP block or control using a computer-generated random sequence, with assignments kept in sealed envelopes until the day of surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence and sealed-envelope allocation were reported, and baseline characteristics were balanced, but the envelopes were not described as opaque or sequentially numbered, leaving concealment incompletely documented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly chosen to receive either ESP plus conventional opioid analgesics... or receive only the conventional opioid analgesics... by a random sequence number generated by the computer kept in sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating clinicians could not be blinded to receipt of the block, allowing co-intervention or behavioral effects, although a standardized analgesic/rescue protocol was reported and all 60 randomized patients appear to have been analyzed as assigned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Since patients know whether or not they have received an injection for ESP block, the placebo effect could not be minimized.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 60 enrolled and allocated participants were represented in the reported analyses, with no post-randomization losses or missing outcome data described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The remaining 60 patients were allocated equally into two groups: ESP (study) group and C (control) group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome, total postoperative morphine consumption, was objectively measured under a common rescue protocol, and postoperative observers were blinded to group assignment; VAS was also assessed consistently across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The observer anaesthesiologist postoperative will be blinded to which group the patient belongs.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and primary and secondary outcomes were identified, but the registration predated enrollment by only about one month and no protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan was provided to exclude selective choice among multiple VAS time points or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was registered on Clinical-Trials.gov and was assigned an NCT number, Clinical-Trials.gov ID NCT03749395.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven by incomplete reporting of sealed-envelope allocation concealment, lack of participant and clinician blinding in a no-sham control design, and insufficient information to rule out selective reporting. Missing data and outcome measurement were judged low risk.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that patients were assigned to the block or control group using computer-generated random numbers, with allocation concealed in opaque envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a computer-generated sequence and opaque-envelope concealment were reported, envelope safeguards were incompletely described and the groups had a statistically significant baseline age imbalance, raising some concern about the randomization process.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were allocated to either block group (group B) or control group (group C) using computer-generated random numbers. Random numbers were concealed using opaque envelopes and were opened just prior to the administration of block... However, the mean age was significantly different between two groups... P = 0.01.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and the block-performing anesthetist were unblinded, and the report does not explicitly describe intention-to-treat analysis, although standardized perioperative care and inclusion of all 60 randomized patients reduce concern about material deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Second, the patient and the anesthetist performing the block were not blinded to the group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear available for all 60 randomized participants, with 30 analyzed in each group and no post-randomization losses reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 60 patients were randomized into two groups... Group B (n=30)... Group C (n=30).

domain_judgments.rationale: Morphine consumption from a standardized PCA device is an appropriate outcome measured similarly between groups, but unblinded patients controlled their own analgesic use, so knowledge of receiving the block could influence the primary outcome despite blinded pain-score assessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: An intravenous patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) pump was used to provide morphine for rescue analgesia in all the patients... The pain score on a numeric rating scale (NRS) was recorded... by an investigator blinded to the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary outcomes and analysis methods are described, but no prospective protocol or trial registration is reported, so selective choice among eligible analyses or outcome specifications cannot be excluded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 24-hour morphine consumption was considered as the primary outcome and secondary outcomes included time to first rescue analgesia, pain scores at 0, ½, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 24 h and characteristics and complications associated with block procedure.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. This is driven by incomplete detail on allocation concealment alongside a chance baseline age imbalance, lack of participant blinding for a patient-controlled analgesic outcome, and absence of a reported prospective protocol or registration; outcome data were nevertheless complete.
